subject: POC trial planning — next steps & workload intake
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmehealth.com>, Laura Green <laura.green@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning — next steps & workload intake

Hi Tom / Laura —

Great to meet you both on the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped and scheduled: 

Summary / success criteria (based on our discussion)
- Integrate Redwood API with your annotation pipeline and validate latency under live traffic (90th p95 target: < 350ms for 512 token end-to-end requests).
- Maintain classification accuracy on our test prompts (baseline F1 >= 0.92 on the 200 sample eval set Acme will provide).
- Demonstrate predictable cost reduction vs current setup via batching/caching (target >= 25% cost savings at target throughput).

POC scope & timeline proposal
- Week 0 (this week): finalize workload intake and success criteria, sign SOW/POC order.
- Week 1: technical kickoff + env setup (API keys, VPC/whitelist if needed, sample data).
- Weeks 2–3: run POC traffic, collect metrics and tune.
- Week 4: evaluation, final report, recommended next steps.

Owners
- Sales/contract: Ben Carter (me) — commercial and SOW.
- Technical/implementation: Marissa Cole — kickoff, infra, and run support.
- Infra sizing & performance: Dylan Brooks — pod sizing, qps estimates.
- Acme side: Tom / Laura — provide eval prompts, baseline metrics, and access to test endpoints.

Workload intake (needed from you to size the environment and confirm plan) — short checklist: 
1) Average RPS (requests per second) during normal operation
2) Expected peak RPS and typical burst duration (e.g., 20 RPS for 1–2 minutes)
3) Average request prompt token length and average completion token length (or 95th-percentile lengths)
4) Typical concurrency (how many parallel sessions/users hitting the endpoint)
5) Traffic pattern (steady vs spiky; time-of-day/week variations)
6) Any SSO/VPN/KMS requirements for private deployment or PII-sensitive data
7) Evaluation dataset (link or sample of ~200 prompts you mentioned)

Attachments: POC-Checklist.pdf (attached) — this is a short template we use to collect the above. I'll also drop a shared Drive link for a workload template.

Can you send the workload numbers and confirm the owners/timeline above? If those look good I'll have Marissa reach out with proposed kickoff slots.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Green <laura.green@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning — next steps & workload intake

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the high level success criteria; below are the workload answers I have now (we'll follow up with a short spreadsheet attached):

- Average RPS: ~2 rps (during business hours).
- Peak RPS: bursts up to ~20 rps for 1–3 minutes (internal syncs / batch ingestion windows).
- Average prompt tokens: 120 tokens (mostly short clinical notes and prompts).
- Average completion tokens: 80 tokens. 95th percentile prompt+completion ~600 tokens.
- Typical concurrency: 3–5 concurrent sessions per service (we have multiple microservices but only one will hit Redwood during the POC).
- Traffic pattern: mostly steady during business hours with short, predictable bursts at 1am UTC for batch jobs (rarely longer than 2–3 mins).
- Security: we will need audit logs and link to our SSO; no air-gapped requirement for the POC.

We'd like to start the POC in ~4 weeks (mid-April) to align with a release. Attached is a short workload summary (acme-workload-summary.xlsx) with sample traces.

Tom Ellis
Senior Product Manager, AI & Data | Acme Health
tom.ellis@acmehealth.com | (617) 555-0123

Tom — perfect, this is really helpful. Quick follow-up notes and next steps: 

- Timeline: mid-April start works. I'll get the SOW and POC order drafted this week (expected turnaround 2–3 business days).
- Security: we will enable audit logging for the POC and integrate with your SSO for API provisioning. Marissa will coordinate the SSO steps.
- Sizing: Dylan — can you confirm the initial pod sizing for the stated patterns (avg 2 rps, burst 20 rps, 95th token ~600)?

Dylan (cc): can you take a quick look and advise initial capacity we should reserve for the Dedicated test pool and whether we recommend using auto-burst for the short 20 rps spikes?

If that looks good I'll schedule the technical kickoff with Marissa. Proposed slots: Tue 2027-04-12 10:00–11:00 PT, Wed 2027-04-13 13:00–14:00 PT, Thu 2027-04-14 09:00–10:00 PT.

Thanks —
Ben

Hi Tom / Ben —

Thanks — I'll own the technical kickoff and runbook for the POC. I've attached our workload intake template (workload-profile-template.xlsx) for you to confirm the numbers in the spreadsheet format we use. For clarity, here are the fields we'll validate during kickoff and the data we need from Acme: 

- Representative request traces (CSV or logs) for 24–72 hours if possible.
- Avg RPS and peak RPS (with timestamps of peaks).
- Request token distribution: avg, median, 90th, 95th, max (prompt and completion).
- Concurrent connections and typical session behavior (long-lived vs short).
- Failure mode: what should trigger failover vs fallback responses.
- Expected SLA targets and any hard limits (p95 latency thresholds, acceptable error rates).
- Data retention / audit log window for the POC.

Next steps I will take after getting the filled template / traces:
1) Validate model selection and quantization profile for cost/perf tradeoffs.
2) Provision a Dedicated test pool sized for steady 2 rps + auto-burst to 25 rps (safety margin) and confirm warm-up time.
3) Share a short test plan and measurement dashboard (latency, errors, tokens, cost).

Kickoff: I'm available for the proposed slots — Tue 2027-04-12 10:00 PT is my preference. Can you confirm?

Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
